newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to speed up foreign holding in Telecom - report.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to speed up foreign holding in Telecom - report.

text.p: South Korea's Finance and Economy Ministry plans to issue overseas depositary receipts in state-run Korea Telecom in the second half of this year and then seek a local listing, local media reported on Sunday.

The Seoul Economic Daily said the ministry had decided on the plan in an attempt to minimise any shock to the domestic stock market and generate government revenue by selling shares in the state-run company.
Government officials were not available to comment.
Korea Telecom, about 80 percent owned by the government, has a monoply on local telephone services and the lion's share of the long-distance call market.

The finance ministry said in May it planned to allow foreign investors to own 20 percent of Korea Telecom from 1998 and 33 percent from 2001. Individual foreign shareholdings were to be limited to three percent.
The daily did not explain why the government decided to allow a foreign shareholding earlier than scheduled.
It said the listing of Korea Telecom on the local market was expected in September or October.

The finance ministry last year had said Korea Telecom would be listed on the Korea Stock Exchange in the first half of 1997. The government has repeatedly postponed listing Korea Telecom since 1995, citing weak stock market conditions.
The government has been selling Korea Telecom shares since 1993 in a move to privatise state-run companies.
